title: Chapter 5: Boss Level 1: The Bill Splitter
video_title: Python Chapter 5: Boss Level 1, The Bill Splitter
summary: Four friends share a cafe bill, and rounding each share costs a cent. Follow Asha as she plans, builds and tests a bill splitter with input, f-strings and whole-cent maths (// and %), using an AI assistant at all six stages and catching two confident AI mistakes with tests worked out by hand.

segments.say: Welcome to Code Quest, Chapter 5. This is your first boss level!
No new topic today. You will build a real tool with everything from Chapters 1 to 4.
segments.subtitle: Plan it. Build it. Test it.

segments.say: And an AI assistant will make two confident mistakes about money. Your tests will catch both.

visual.heading: Four friends, one bill
visual.label: The problem
items: The bill is 37.45, plus a 15% tip. The receipt says 43.07.
A phone calculator says each friend pays **10.7675**.
Nobody can pay 10.7675. So each friend pays **10.77**.

segments.say: Four friends finish lunch at the Corner Cafe. The bill is 37.45. With a 15 percent tip, the receipt says 43.07, to the cent.
One friend divides 43.07 by 4 on a phone calculator. Each person pays 10.7675.
Nobody can pay that. So they round it, and each friend pays 10.77.
So how much do they pay together?

ask.question: Four friends each pay 10.77. How much do they pay together?

after.say: 43.08. That is one cent more than the real total, 43.07. Somebody paid a cent too much, and nobody knows who.
Small? Yes. But a cafe serves hundreds of tables. Asha wants a tool that gets it right every time.

visual.heading: Build a fair bill splitter
visual.label: The mission
items: Ask three questions: the bill, the tip percent, the number of people.
Print a neat receipt with the bill, the tip and the total.
Tell each person exactly what to pay.
Say how many cents are left over, so the table can decide who pays them.

segments.say: Here is the mission. Asha's tool asks three questions: the bill, the tip percent and the number of people.
It prints a neat receipt, like the one from Chapter 3.
It tells each person exactly what to pay.
And if the money does not share out evenly, it says how many cents are left over.

scenes.title: Acceptance criteria
scenes.direction: Six criteria, revealed one by one. Then a quiz on the types, then a breather.

visual.heading: Done means all six are true
visual.label: Acceptance criteria
items: Asks for the bill, the tip percent and the number of people.
The bill can have decimals. The tip percent and people are whole numbers.
Shows the bill, the tip and the total with two decimal places, in one column.
Shows what each person pays, rounded down to a whole cent.
Shows the extra cents. Shares plus extra cents equal the total exactly.
Passes at least four tests worked out by hand.

segments.say: Before building, Asha writes down what done means. These are called acceptance criteria. The tool is finished when all six are true.
One. It asks the three questions, in this order.
Two. The bill can have decimals, like 37.45. The tip percent and the number of people are whole numbers.
Three. Money shows two decimal places, lined up.
Four. Each share is rounded down to a whole cent.
Five. The extra cents are shown, so the shares and the extra cents add up to the total exactly.
And six. It passes at least four tests that you worked out by hand.

after.say: A. The bill total. It can have decimals. The other two are whole numbers, so they use int.

scenes.title: Plan it with AI
scenes.direction: Stage 1 plan, then Asha adds the whole-cents step, then stage 2: she writes the questions and asks the AI to check them.

messages.text: I am a beginner. I know print, variables, int and float, the operators including // and %, f-strings and input. I want a program that splits a cafe bill between friends with a tip. Do not write code. List the inputs, the calculations in order and the outputs.

Inputs: the bill total (`float`), the tip percent (`int`) and the number of people (`int`).
Calculations: the tip, then the total, then each share: the total divided by the people.
Outputs: the bill, the tip, the total and each share, with two decimal places.

segments.say: Stage 1: plan. Asha tells the AI what she knows, and what she wants. And she says: no code yet.
The AI lists the inputs with their types, the calculations in order, and the outputs. It is a good plan.
But look at the last calculation: each share is the total, divided by the people. That is exactly what the phone calculator did.

items: 43.07 divided by 4 is 10.7675: not a real amount of money.
So work in **whole cents**: 43.07 is 4307 cents.
Whole cents share out with `//`, and `%` gives the cents left over.

segments.say: Asha remembers the mission. 43.07 divided by 4 is 10.7675, and nobody can pay that.

Line 5: `int`, because you cannot have half a person.

scenes.title: Step 2: The tip, with AI
scenes.direction: Teach the percent rule first. Then stage 3 plants the AI mistake and the learner judges it; stage 4 tests against the hand result.

visual.heading: Step 2: What is 10 percent?
visual.label: Build it
body: A percent is a number **out of 100**.
10 percent of 48 is 48 times 10, divided by 100: **4.80**.

segments.say: Step 2: the tip. First, the maths. A percent is a number out of 100.
So 10 percent of 48 is 48 times 10, divided by 100. That is 4.80. Asha works this out by hand, before any code.

visual.heading: Generate: two lines, with a prediction

messages.text: Write the lines that calculate the tip and the total for a bill of 48 with a 10 percent tip. Use the names bill, tip_percent, tip and total. Tell me what they print.
Here are the lines. They print `Tip: 4.80` and `Total: 52.80`.

segments.say: Stage 3: generate. Asha asks the AI for the tip and total lines, and asks what they print.
The AI writes a few short lines, and says they print a tip of 4.80. It sounds sure.
Read line 4 carefully.

ask.question: The AI says this prints `Tip: 4.80`. Is it right?

after.say: No. Line 4 multiplies by 10, and never divides by 100. Let's see what really happens.

visual.heading: Test: compare with the result you worked out

messages.text: I worked it out by hand first: 10 percent of 48 is 4.80. Your lines printed this:
Line 4 multiplies the bill by 10, not by 10 percent. A percent must be divided by 100:

segments.say: Stage 4: test. Asha runs the lines. The tip is 480! Ten times bigger than the whole bill. Her hand result catches it immediately.
She shows the AI the real output. This time it names the cause: a percent must be divided by 100.
She runs the fix. 4.80, and a total of 52.80. Now the code and her hand result agree.

scenes.title: Step 3: Share in whole cents
scenes.direction: The cents lines type in one by one, each explained. The learner predicts the check line, then the reveal. Then a quiz on remainders.

visual.heading: Step 3: Share the total in whole cents

segments.say: Step 3, the most important part. Asha uses the mission's numbers: a total of 43.07, and 4 people.
Line 4 multiplies by 100 to get cents. It uses round, because a float can be a tiny amount below the whole number you expect.
Line 5 shares the cents with double slash: whole cents only.
Line 6 uses the remainder operator to find the cents left over.
Lines 7 to 9 print the three numbers. And line 10 is a check: each share times the people, plus the extra cents.

ask.question: If no cent is lost, what must the check on line 10 print?

after.say: 4307, the total in cents. And it does! Every cent is accounted for.
Each person pays 1076 cents, and 3 cents are left over.

visual.question: Seven people share 100 cents. How many extra cents are left over?

segments.say: Quick check. Seven people share 100 cents. How many extra cents are left over?

after.say: C, 2. Each person gets 14 cents. 14 times 7 is 98, and 2 cents are left.

scenes.title: Step 4: Back to money
scenes.direction: Short beat: why .2f matters for money.

visual.heading: Step 4: Turn cents back into money

segments.say: Step 4. To show money again, divide the cents by 100. 1760 cents becomes 17.6.
Line 4 prints 17.6. Python drops the last zero of a float.
Line 5 adds dot 2 f, so it looks like money: 17.60.
And line 6 puts it in a receipt line: 16 characters for the label, 8 for the amount.

visual.heading: Debug: a test that breaks the program

messages.text: A friend typed 0 for the number of people, and the program stopped. Here are the lines and the full error. Explain the cause first. Then suggest the smallest fix I can make with what I know.

Line 10 divides by `people`, which is 0. Nothing can be shared between zero people, so Python stops with a `ZeroDivisionError`.
For now, make the question clear: `Number of people (1 or more): `. Checking the answer needs `if`, which comes later.

segments.say: Stage 5: debug. A friend tries to break the tool, and types 0 for the number of people. The program stops with an error. Asha reads it: line 10.
Asha pastes the lines and the full error, and asks for the cause first. The AI explains: nothing can be shared between zero people.
To refuse a bad answer, the program must make a decision. That needs if, which you meet in Chapter 6. For now, a clear question helps.

scenes.title: Improve it with AI
scenes.direction: Stage 6: the AI suggests rounding each share. The learner judges it, then the test on its own screen. Then the six stages, a quiz and a breather.

messages.text: My splitter passes all four tests. Suggest one way to make it simpler. Do not change what it prints.
Replace the two share lines, 10 and 12, with one line: `share = round(total / people, 2)`. It is shorter and gives the same result.

segments.say: Stage 6: improve. Asha asks for one way to make the program simpler, without changing what it prints.
The AI suggests replacing the two share lines, 10 and 12, with one line: round the total divided by the people, to 2 places.
Shorter, yes. Think about the mission before you answer.

ask.question: The AI says one rounded line gives the same result. Is it right?

after.say: Asha does not guess. She tests it with the mission's numbers.

segments.say: Line 4 is the AI's line. Line 6 adds up the four shares.
Each pays 10.77, and the shares add up to 43.08. One cent too much: the exact problem from the mission!
So Asha keeps her cent lines. A suggestion that changes the result is not a simplification.
Here are all six stages on one tool.
The AI helped every time. It planned, checked, wrote, explained and suggested.
And it was wrong twice: the tip, and the rounding.
Both times, a test caught it. The same test you work out by hand.
